title: Chapter 60
content:
When the three sat down for dinner, the table groaned beneath a feast so extravagant it looked ready to snap its legs. A rich spread blending authentic Chinese specialties and Korean delicacies made it immediately clear just how much effort had gone into the meal. Il-hyun had discreetly absented himself to spare them the discomfort, but even without his presence, dining under this roof felt no less suffocating.

"Master Yi-an—ah, no. Calling you by your real name feels a bit strange. In any case, it is wonderful to see you back."

The senior housekeeper welcomed him with a warm, maternal smile, asking zero probing questions. But Jakyeong couldn't bring himself to trust the woman anymore. A kindly old lady who could calmly bury a severed human head in the backyard with a gentle smile was hardly ordinary. Letting her remind him of Wang Han’s late grandmother had been a foolish lapse in judgment.

The moment she stepped out of the dining room, Wang Ryun leaned in, whispering under his breath:

"Is it safe to eat? You sure it isn't laced with something?"

After a brief hesitation, Wang Han took the first bite, nodding in quiet appreciation. Ryun and Jakyeong dug in immediately after. Sure enough, the taste was as extraordinary as the aroma. Having starved for four days straight, Jakyeong devoured the food in silence. Earlier, his blinding fury had masked his physical hunger, but now the hollow ache in his stomach struck with a vengeance. Whether by Il-hyun’s deliberate instruction or not, not a single domestic servant lingered in sight while they ate.

Finishing dinner, the trio gathered in the second-floor lounge. A heavy silence stretched over the table as steam rose from their teacups. At Il-hyun’s insistence, they had agreed to spend the night, but their thoughts remained tangled. The proposal to wire the entire retainer upfront in a single lump sum had split the room in two.

Wang Han remained firmly skeptical, while Wang Ryun was all for taking the deal without a second thought. Flipping one's stance for cash might seem shallow, but in their trade, money was absolute. Capital could buy a life or end one—and there was nothing more formidable than that.

"Jakyeong, what do you think?"

Jakyeong couldn't reach a verdict. Being tethered to one location for an entire year was bad enough, but having Kang Il-hyun as his employer was deeply unsettling. A client who had attempted betrayal once was bound to do it again—the very reason he had severed ties with Dmitri. Yet setting all risks aside, the payout was colossal enough to test any man's resolve.

"What if we just take the upfront money and vanish?"

The casual remark drew twin stares from Han and Ryun. Ryun scratched the bridge of his nose, hesitating.

"By the way... did you really sleep with that guy...?"

Before Ryun could finish, Han kicked his shin under the table. Watching the meaningful glances passing between them, Jakyeong’s eyes narrowed into sharp slits. He knew exactly where Ryun’s mind was wandering.

"I told you, it's not like that."

Ryun grinned. "Hey, I don't judge. Love is love."

Han raised a hand in solidarity. "Same here." Still, the idea of the partner being Kang Il-hyun sat poorly with him. Male or female didn't matter, but Han had always hoped their youngest would find someone warm, kind, and generous who would shower him with genuine affection.

Seeing their unconvinced expressions, Jakyeong realized further denials would only make him look guiltier. Cornered, he gave a reluctant nod.

"It was a one-time mistake. End of story. Don't bring it up again."

Wang Han let out a quiet sigh, while Wang Ryun shook his head in sheer, reverent awe.

"Unbelievable... To think a ruthless bastard like Kang Il-hyun let you take him from behind."

Jakyeong’s face contorted in sheer horror. I knew he'd assume that. He opened and closed his mouth, at a complete loss for words. Catching the panic, Han shot Ryun a sharp glare to shut him up, but Ryun kept marveling at Jakyeong's supposed prowess until Jakyeong threw his hands up and surged to his feet.

"I'm going to bed. We'll talk tomorrow."

As Jakyeong bolted out the door like a hunted animal, Ryun turned to Han with a chuckle. "Look at him blush. How cute."

Han clicked his tongue, shaking his head. "You're infuriating in every way, Ryun, but your complete lack of tact is easily your worst quality."

Stepping into his old guest suite, Jakyeong took in the room. A full year had passed, yet practically nothing had changed. He eyed the freshly laundered sheets and pillows before walking over to the panoramic window. After days of relentless storming, the night sky was crystal-clear.

The pool below remained unchanged, the matching sun loungers sat in their exact spots, and the surrounding foliage had grown noticeably lusher. Outside, the perimeter guards were stationed far more heavily than before. Is he still facing active assassination threats?

Jakyeong sparked a cigarette. Exhaling against the cool glass, the gray plume clouded the reflection before dissipating. His mind grew heavier by the second. The figures written across that contract kept replaying in his head. It was more than enough to buy the private island he'd been eyeing—and furnish it lavishly. If the employer were anyone other than Kang Il-hyun, he would have signed on the dotted line without a heartbeat's hesitation.

His dark gaze drifted down to his bare heels before tracking all the way back up to lock onto Jakyeong's face.

"Get out." Jakyeong turned his head the other way with a dismissive scowl.

Il-hyun walked over and sat on the edge of the mattress. The black viper tattoo coiled across Jakyeong's shoulder blade was striking. A cat would have suited him so much better. Remembering he had thought the exact same thing a year ago, Il-hyun briefly regretted not having the tattoo artist cover it while the boy was sedated.

Faint purple bruises from their scuffle in the basement mottled the pale skin.

"You bruise easily."

Jakyeong rolled his head back to glare. The swelling on Il-hyun's jaw had already subsided after a bit of ice. It felt infuriatingly unfair—a lingering sense of defeat that churned his gut.

Holding Jakyeong's venomous stare, Il-hyun spoke with sudden, quiet gravity.
